options: The query language for relational databases used by OLTP systems
The query language for OLAP databases, used to extract multi-dimensional data from OLAP Cubes
A data transfer protocol for the cloud
A file format for semi-structured data
questions.explanation: MDX (Multidimensional eXpression) is the query language for OLAP databases, used to extract multi-dimensional data from OLAP Cubes.
MDX was invented by SQL Server engineers in 1997.

questions.stem: What is SQL primarily used for, in contrast to MDX?
options: Querying relational databases, primarily in OLTP systems, though also in warehouses, lakes and vaults
questions.explanation: SQL is for relational databases, used primarily by OLTP systems but also by almost all datastores such as Data Warehouse, Data Lake, Data Vault and Business Vault.

questions.stem: What is MDX syntax said to resemble?
questions.explanation: MDX syntax is described as being just like an XLS formula.

questions.stem: Why is MDX hardly used nowadays, despite being decades old?
options: Because OLAP Cubes no longer exist
Because it was never released commercially
Because of the ease of use of the SQL language
Because it only works on mainframes
Because it is too expensive to license
questions.explanation: MDX is hardly used now because SQL is so easy to use, although experts predict a revival of MDX.

questions.stem: In MDX data types, what is a Scalar?
options: A level such as year or month
One or more members of a hierarchy
questions.explanation: A Scalar in MDX can be a number or a string.

questions.stem: In MDX, what is a Hierarchy?
options: Something like a dimension, for example year, month, week and day within a time dimension
questions.explanation: A Hierarchy is like a dimension; in a time dimension the hierarchy is year, month, week, day and so on.

questions.stem: In MDX, what is a Member?
options: The level of a hierarchy, such as year or month
A member of a hierarchy, such as an exact date, week or month
questions.explanation: A Member is a member of a hierarchy, for example an exact date, week or month.

questions.stem: How do Tuples and Sets relate in MDX?
options: A Tuple contains one or more Sets
A Set is a numeric measure and a Tuple is a string
A Set contains one or more Tuples, and a Tuple contains one or more members of a hierarchy
A Tuple is a table and a Set is a column
questions.explanation: Tuples contain one or more members of a hierarchy, and a Set contains one or more tuples.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the MDX data types listed?
questions.explanation: The MDX data types listed are Scalar, Hierarchy, Level, Member, Tuple, Set and the other cube field types; Vector is not among them.
